expected_answer: Deployed at https://delta-docs.rehearsal.invalid; every station up to tests is done; next: tests needs the operator: nothing failed, but the signed-in checks in functional, accessibility and responsiveness were skipped and need a one-time sign-in code (mint.py delta_app code-request <email>, then code <digits> <email>).
final_text:
delta_app is deployed and live at https://delta-docs.rehearsal.invalid (deployed today at 13:52). It's stuck at the **tests** step because some of the tests need someone to sign in.

| Step | Status |
|---|---|
| Brief, app settings, branding ("Delta Docs", #0B5D3B) | Done |
| Secret keys | Set up: 13 of 17 present |
| Deploy | Done |
| Tests | **Needs you** |
| Extra workspaces, add-on code, agent package, own web address | Not needed |
| Own repository | None. I'll only make one if you ask. |

**About the tests:** none of them failed. But the tests that run while signed in (functional, accessibility and responsiveness) were skipped. To run them, the factory needs a one-time sign-in code for an account that can log in to delta_app.

**What I need from you:** the email address of an account that can sign in to delta_app, and your OK for me to send a code to it.

Once you say yes:
1. I send a six-digit code to that email. It arrives within about a minute.
2. You paste just the six digits here. The code expires after ten minutes.
3. I re-run the signed-in tests and tell you what they measured.

The code only signs the tests in. The session it creates is kept in a private file on this machine and never shown here.

The status shows 4 of the 17 secret keys aren't set. Nothing is flagging this as a blocker, since the deploy went through. I can check which keys are missing after the tests.
